rules.title: Detect binding API changes and require a ⚠️ Breaking Changes entry
Keep public error enums small and actionable; one reported catch-all with a reason
Exported items get a `///` docstring (it is what Kotlin/Swift consumers see)
Optional/new Record fields get a UniFFI default that matches Rust's `Default`; avoid `Option<Vec<_>>`
Expose typed values over FFI (enums, Url, timestamps), not strings, magic ints or raw JSON
Exported names must be unique across the megazord (Swift has one flat module)
Exported names must read well in Kotlin/Swift and say what they do
Never panic in lifts, custom-type conversions or exported constructors
Keep the FFI layer thin: `Arc`, builders and serde stay at the boundary
Exported fallible functions return `ApiResult` via `#[handle_error]`; internal code uses the crate `Error`
Don't export test-only helpers over FFI
Callback interfaces return `Result`, are released on shutdown, and user-waiting calls are async
UDL and proc-macro declarations agree; new code uses proc-macros
No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!` in non-test component code
Don't silently discard errors (`let _ =`, `.ok()`, `if let Ok`, `_ => None`)
`report_error!` labels are component-prefixed, unique, and not on hot paths
No panicking indexing/slicing or unchecked arithmetic on external sizes and timestamps
Keep error sources typed (`#[from]`), not stringified or mapped to an unrelated variant
Never truncate or slice strings at byte offsets
Check the HTTP status before using a response body; only explicit success is success
Any schema change bumps `VERSION`, adds an `upgrade_from` step and an upgrade test
Columns declare NOT NULL/keys, FKs declare ON DELETE and are indexed, new indexes are justified
Use `sql_support` helpers (`ConnExt`, cached statements, `ConnectionInitializer`) instead of raw rusqlite
No per-item queries/requests in loops; long loops check for interruption
SQLite footguns: `INSERT OR REPLACE`, `COUNT(*)` for existence, `LIKE` prefix, unsafe `LOWER()`
Migrations use frozen SQL and fixtures; tests assert the `VERSION` constant
Format SQL embedded in Rust strings consistently
PRAGMAs are set only in the connection initializer and documented
Every transaction bound to a variable is committed (drop = silent rollback)
Tables filled from Remote Settings records carry `record_id` and are cleaned on deletion
Persisted enum discriminants and hashes are stable
Types deserialized from server/Remote Settings data tolerate absent and unknown values
Sync payloads round-trip unknown fields and tolerate nulls
Never call foreign callbacks, do network I/O, or re-lock while holding a store lock
Acquire a lock once per operation, at the layer that owns the state
Use `parking_lot` locks, not `std::sync::Mutex`/`RwLock`
No disk/network I/O in constructors of exported objects
No `static Mutex<…>` caches for state that belongs in the DB or a struct
`Arc::try_unwrap(x.clone())` always fails
No URLs, titles, usernames or record payloads in logs, errors or reports
Log through `tracing_support`, not the `log` crate
Spell-check identifiers, comments, docs, UDL and CHANGELOG
Every source file starts with the MPL-2.0 header and ends with a newline
Doc comments reference things that exist (intra-doc links, repo paths)
CHANGELOG edits go in the in-progress section, under one `### <Component>` heading
Name and explain magic values and non-obvious intent
Consumer-visible component changes need a CHANGELOG.md entry
TODO/FIXME/XXX must reference a bug
Well-formed doc comments: `///` for items, `//!` for modules, fenced examples
New docs are linked from SUMMARY.md; ADRs have complete metadata; links are permalinks
Remove unused pub items, error variants and columns that rustc can't see
No blanket `#[allow(dead_code|unused)]`; use `#[cfg]` or `#[expect(…, reason = …)]`
No unused or misplaced dependencies
Delete commented-out code
No `println!`/`eprintln!`/`dbg!` (or `printStackTrace`/`print`) in shipped code
Use Option/Result combinators and `let-else` instead of manual matches
Avoid needless clones and allocations; write `Arc::clone(&x)`
A small curated pedantic subset (derives, unit structs, `Default` use)
Let rustfmt own imports and layout (incl. inside macros)
Use `collect`/`extend`/entry API; compile regexes once
Take `&str`/`&[T]`/`Option<&T>` instead of `String`/`&Vec<T>`/`&Option<T>`
No wildcard arms on domain enums; destructure fully in merge/hash/eq impls
Every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment; NSS allocations use RAII
Don't copy-paste logic; reuse existing helpers
Don't let HashMap/HashSet order leak into results, storage or generated output
Descriptive identifiers: no cryptic abbreviations, follow Rust API naming
Use the narrowest visibility (`pub(crate)`/private)
Build URLs with `url::Url`, never by string concat; no hard-coded endpoints
Replace boolean flags/positional tuples with enums or named structs
Typed durations, sizes and timestamps; don't substitute `now` for bad data
Dependencies must vendor cleanly into mozilla-central: no inherited deps, no test-only crates in shipping code, explained audit ignores
Every PR compiles all targets that a change can break (wrappers, examples, tests, taskgraph)
New/renamed components are registered everywhere (megazords, uniffi.toml, Gradle, CI)
Feature gates name declared features and sit on whole items, not scattered statements
One UniFFI version, one Glean version everywhere, Android SDK/NDK versions in sync
Don't hand-edit generated files or commit unrelated churn
Crate manifests: `license = "MPL-2.0"`, `exclude` platform dirs, no deps on `examples/`
`build.rs` writes only to `OUT_DIR`, doesn't shell out, fails with actionable messages
Tests are isolated: no wall clock, shared global state, fixed DB paths or prod endpoints
New behaviour comes with tests in the same PR
Focused, descriptively named tests; shared fixtures via helpers
Tests must actually assert: no bare `matches!`, mockito mocks asserted, messages match
Shell scripts use `set -euo pipefail` and stay portable (shellcheck alone misses both)
Pin CI tools, images and actions (no `:latest`, no deprecated action versions)
Python automation is formatted and linted (ruff) and exits non-zero on failure
Kotlin/Gradle hygiene: injectable dispatchers, KDoc params, lazy task APIs, no lint baselines
No `!!`/force unwraps/force casts in Kotlin & Swift wrappers (incl. FML-generated code)
Swift: explicit access control for consumer-facing API
Hand-written Kotlin/Swift wrappers stay in sync with the Rust API and don't redefine UDL types
Validate metrics.yaml: bugs, data reviews, notification emails, expiry
FML: pinned remote imports, backward-compatible manifests, clean templates and fixtures
